doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
title: Callers about Leon Kelner and Ted Andrews's compliment
summary: A caller asks how long Leon Kelner has played the Roosevelt; Ted Andrews praises Pete's civic cooperation and Jack Sperling's missed visit.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players

blocks.x: Thank you, sir. Pete Fountain and Eddie Miller are with us tonight. 522-3791 is the number. Let's take a phone call and see what happens to you fellas. Go ahead, please. You're on the air. Good evening, Doug. Hi.
Doug, how about keep those two recordings and play them quite often? They both sound mighty good.
Well, all right. Well, I'll pass that on to the disc jockeys.

I want to ask Mr. Pete a question. Mr. Pete, how long has Leon Kellner been playing in the Roosevelt Hotel? How long has that man been playing music over there? I've been unable to get an answer. I asked several people and say they don't know.
Well, the trombone player that's working with me now, Jack Delaney, worked with him for, oh, I'd say almost 10 years. And I'd say he's been here at least 25 years.
At least that long, because I remember hearing that man on the radio playing music at least 25 years ago.

Well, I know when I was working with Basin Street 6, he was at the Roosevelt, but he would come in and out. That's when they were using different bands. He was like the house band. But he would come in and out more than anybody else.
Well, look, Kevin, thank you. Thank you very much. Thank you, sir.
Thanks for your call. Hello. Go ahead, please.

This is Ted Andrews, Doug. Hi. I would like to compliment Pete on a couple of things that possibly a lot of people don't know about. Number one, I've had occasion to work with Pete or ask him favors in a promotional way for New Orleans. We all know that he loves New Orleans. But I've never seen anyone as cooperative that would go out of his way to do things for sports, for a baseball club, for anything that you ask him to do and just take his time out to do it. And Pete's been that kind of a guy all the way through. And just tell him that I hear from Tex Panicki right often, and Tex is coming in here, I think, from Mardi Gras. And, of course, Tex used to come in and see Shecky Green and Pete Pountain, and now all he talks about is Pete Pountain. So when Tex comes in, if we could get Jack Spurling back here,

we'd have a good jam session. Jack was supposed to come in. Believe it or not, I got a call from him last night. He couldn't make it. He couldn't get out of a NBC staff show he had to do. But he was going to come in for the weekend. Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. We're sure going to miss him, though. Yeah, well, he's quite a government. Fantastic, man. And thank you. I hope my wife has listened to what you said.
